assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of 1e-18 systematic uncertainty, is a clear, concrete advance in atomic precision measurement. It opened tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a prospective redefinition of the second. The atomic-structure physics behind the magic wavelength and blackbody-shift control is the kind of work I can judge directly.
assessment.attribution: Katori conceived the lattice-clock idea and magic wavelength; Ye's group drove the strontium clock to record accuracy and stability. The two-name configuration is natural and does not appear to need a third laureate, though ion-clock and Sr-clock competitors exist.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many independent groups, with stable interpretation and long maturity; recognition is timely, as the 2005 comb prize left the clock application itself unrecognised.
uncertainties: Whether the clock achievement is distinct enough from the frequency-comb prize and from ion clocks (Wineland 2012) is a judgement call.
Roles of other lattice-clock groups (e.g., at PTB, NIST, SYRTE) are not captured in the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model predicted flat bands at the magic angle, and the 2018 experiments revealed correlated insulators and superconductivity. This created a whole field of moire quantum matter with a clean, tunable platform. Originality and impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Theory (Bistritzer, MacDonald) and experiment (Jarillo-Herrero) form a natural triple. Cao and Fatemi, first authors on the experiments, and other contributors (e.g., Dean, Young, Kim) are outside the credited list, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed independently by many groups across several moire systems; the mechanism of superconductivity remains debated, but the discovery itself is secure. Timing is fairly early but plausible.
uncertainties: MacDonald also appears under another entry (quantum Hall bilayers) with credit dispersed across moire work by other theorists.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the subsequent theory of quantum simulation with cold atoms and ions is foundational to the AMO route to quantum information. It is original, precise and was rapidly turned into experiment, and its reach across platforms is wide.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are clearly the decisive theorists on the two-name proposal; the credit is clean. Experimental realisation by Wineland, Blatt and others partially overlaps with the 2012 prize.
assessment.maturity: Two decades of independent experimental confirmation across ions, neutral atoms and Rydberg arrays. Mature and timely, as quantum-information science is widely recognised.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) and with the neighbouring cold-atom simulation entry could make the scope hard to define.
The theory-only character may weigh against it relative to experimental breakthroughs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The experimental discovery of the Higgs boson completed the Standard Model and was one of the major measurements in the field. The 2013 prize recognised the theory, so the experimental discovery remains unrecognised and the importance is not in doubt.
assessment.attribution: The collaboration-scale discovery is hard to attribute to three individuals; I weigh the spokespersons and CMS leadership as a convenient but imperfect proxy. The choice among Gianotti, Della Negra, Jenni and Virdee is unresolved and the statutes' limit on three laureates and on organisations is a real obstacle.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: confirmed by two experiments and a decade of coupling measurements. Recognition is long overdue only in the sense that the attribution problem has prevented it.
uncertainties: Attribution to individuals for a several-thousand-person collaboration is disputed and may be unworkable.
I am not an expert in collider experiments and defer to my colleagues on credit allocation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-particle Penning-trap measurements by Gabrielse and the trapping and spectroscopy of antihydrogen by ALPHA offer precision tests of CPT and the matter-antimatter symmetry. The atomic-physics content, including 1S-2S spectroscopy of antihydrogen, is impressive and of lasting interest.
assessment.attribution: The two names reasonably capture antiproton/positron trapping and antihydrogen spectroscopy, though ATHENA/ATRAP (Gabrielse led ATRAP) and the earlier Penning-trap work by Dehmelt and Van Dyck are relevant. Fair allocation could be contested.
assessment.maturity: Antihydrogen results are confirmed by ALPHA, ASACUSA and ATRAP; precision is still improving, but no violation found. Likely timely but possibly early in terms of fundamental payoff.
uncertainties: Absence of an observed symmetry violation limits the discovery narrative.
Credit between the ATHENA, ATRAP and ALPHA collaborations is not fully resolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) by Hosono's group and rapid Tc increases to above 50 K opened the second family of high-temperature superconductors. Its impact on correlated-electron physics has been broad and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the original discovery; Chen and Zhao contributed to the quick rise of Tc in related compounds. The allocation to the second and third names is reasonably supportable, though many groups contributed in the first months.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed; the pairing mechanism remains debated and no room-temperature application has emerged. Timing is acceptable after 18 years.
uncertainties: Hosono's role is clear but others' marginal contributions are harder to separate.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect, theory by Kane and Mele and the HgTe experiment by Molenkamp's group, gave a new classification of quantum matter. The importance extends from fundamental to application-oriented work.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are the theoretical originators; Molenkamp led the first experimental realisation, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicting the HgTe case, which is not in the credited list. The configuration is plausible but leaves a notable gap.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by ARPES of 3D topological insulators and transport; stable interpretation and mature. Recognition seems timely though topology was already honoured in 2016.
uncertainties: The relative weight of Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang prediction is not reflected in the credited names.
Overlap in spirit with the 2016 prize may reduce priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The three-step recollision model is the conceptual basis of high-harmonic generation and attosecond science. It converted a surprising experimental observation into a simple quantum-classical picture. I regard it as important, but I also note that its main applications were recognised by the 2023 prize.
assessment.attribution: Corkum's semiclassical model is the best-known; Lewenstein's quantum treatment and Schafer's contributions are also decisive. I disclose long collaboration in this area (the same community, including L'Huillier's group); I am assessing this on its scientific merit but may be less neutral, so I keep it at the bottom of my eight.
assessment.maturity: Mature and confirmed by countless experiments. Timing is arguable because the 2023 prize already honoured the experimental and attosecond branch, so remaining recognition is uncertain.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 prize may make a new award for the model hard to justify.
Possible conflict of interest due to proximity to the research community.
